note: One row of a released tensor, two ways: the raw PTQ1_0 blocks as the file stores them, and the same row from the F16 GGUF of the same checkpoint, read over an HTTP range request. They are equal element for element, and the only byte that ever differs is the sign of zero -- the F16 file stores -0.0 where the trit is 0 (f16_neg_zero_count), the decode produces +0.0 -- so f16_row_sha256 is over the row with the sign of zero cleared, as fp32 little-endian. Equal to the last bit everywhere else is what proves the packing, the stage walk, the qh parity and the row addressing together, and it says the F16 file is the ternary weights stored as f16 rather than an unquantized model the ternary one approximates.
example_note: One row of the released `blk.0.ffn_gate.weight` in three files: the two pack files of the ternary checkpoint and the F16 GGUF (`f16_hex`, one fp16 per element, little-endian, read over an HTTP range request).  Both packs decode to the same 5120 numbers and those numbers are the F16 row element for element; the only byte that ever differs is the sign of zero -- the F16 file stores -0.0 where the quantized level is 0, every decoder here produces +0.0 -- so `f16_row_sha256` in the cases below is over the row with the sign of zero cleared, as fp32 little-endian.  Equal to the last bit everywhere else is what proves the packing, the block walk, the `qh` parity and the row addressing together, and it says the F16 file is the ternary weights stored as f16 rather than an unquantized model the ternary one approximates.
